A university town that grows its own companies

Colorado State University reported a record enrollment of 34,412 students in fall 2025, and the school reported a record $622 million in sponsored research spending in fiscal 2025. That research does not stay on campus. CSU STRATA, which combined CSU Ventures with the Colorado State University Research Foundation, started a Lab to Life venture studio with help from a U.S. Department of Commerce grant, with a stated goal of launching 15 new companies in three years.

A spin-off like that usually needs a website before it has revenue: something that explains the technology in plain English, says who is behind it, and gives a partner or investor a reason to email. Around those startups sit the businesses every college town relies on, from student housing services to tutors, repair shops, electricians and accountants.

Fort Collins website design starts with the place names

The Census Bureau estimated the city's population at 170,376 in 2023, and customers here describe location by the stretch of town they know. A page that uses those names gives searchers and Google something concrete.

Old Town

The historic downtown, packed with independent shops, restaurants and bars. The City of Fort Collins history site says Disneyland's Main Street U.S.A. drew on Old Town, based on the account of Harper Goff, a Disney designer who grew up here and photographed its buildings. Fort Collins is also known for its craft breweries. Old Town sites need hours, a map and photos that match the storefront.

Campus West and Midtown on College Avenue

Student-heavy blocks west of campus, and the long commercial run of College Avenue through Midtown. Customers here are often new to town each fall, so they search by category and by distance, not by name.

Harmony Road and south Fort Collins

Shopping centers, medical offices and newer neighborhoods. Service businesses here draw from both Fort Collins and the towns to the south and east.

Loveland, Windsor and Timnath

Many trades and home services work all of these. A short, honest paragraph about each town you serve beats a list of twenty suburb names pasted in the footer.

Web design in Fort Collins when the competition is an hour south

Denver agencies can buy ads and write pages that mention Fort Collins, but they are rarely as specific as an owner who works here. That specificity is the advantage to press. A plumber on Harmony Road should say which neighborhoods get same-day service. A tutor near campus should name the courses students actually struggle with. A bike shop in Old Town should list the brands and repairs it handles. Those details are what make a search result relevant to the person typing it.

  1. Pick the searches you can win.Your service plus Fort Collins, plus the nearby towns you really serve. Pro includes ten city pages, each researched and written from scratch.
  2. Keep the facts matched everywhere.Name, address, phone and hours identical on the site and on your Google Business Profile. Pro includes Business Profile setup.
  3. Answer real questions on the page.The questions customers ask you on the phone belong on the site, in your words.
  4. Make contacting you one tap.Call button, a short form that emails every lead, and a map that opens directions.

What each package means for a Fort Collins business

Starter, at $497 one time, is five hand-written pages (home, services, about, contact and service area), live in 7 to 14 days, and fits most single-location shops. Pro, at $997, adds a 10-page site, a photo gallery, local SEO, your Google reviews on the site, the ten city pages and an AI chat widget that is free for 14 days and then $297 a month if you keep it. Agency, at $1,997, starts with keyword research across your whole service area and adds custom design plus AI phone agent setup; the agent is free for 7 days and then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time, separate from the one-time price. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month unless you keep an AI agent. We do not sell page counts: thirty useful pages beat a hundred thin ones.

Help Fort Collins owners can get for free

  • Larimer Small Business Development Center. Hosted by Front Range Community College at its South Shields Street campus, with no-cost, confidential one-on-one advising and low- or no-cost workshops.
  • City of Fort Collins Economic Health Office. Its Business Connectors give free guidance in English and Spanish and point owners to the right city and partner programs.
  • Fort Collins Area Chamber of Commerce. A membership group for area businesses that holds a yearly event celebrating small business.

Common questions

How much does Fort Collins website design cost?

Prices around Northern Colorado range from a cheap builder subscription to agency projects quoted after several meetings. Ours are fixed: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997, paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent with us. The free demo comes first, so you know what you are buying.

Do I need a web developer in Fort Collins or a web designer?

If you need a site that explains your business, ranks for local searches and brings in calls and form leads, a designer who builds is enough, and that is what we do. If you need custom software, user accounts, a web app or a full online store, look for a web developer; those are not in our packages.

Is Fort Collins web development different for a university spin-off?

Often, yes. A young company coming out of campus research may need a site that speaks to investors, partners and future hires before it has a single customer, with plain explanations of the technology and a clear contact path. That is writing work more than code. If the company needs a product dashboard or a login portal, that part belongs with a developer.

Can a small Fort Collins business really outrank Denver agencies and chains?

For searches with Fort Collins in them, or searches made by people in Fort Collins, you have an edge Denver firms cannot copy: you are actually here. Google says local results weigh relevance, distance and prominence. A site that clearly names your town, your streets and your services helps with the first two. No one can promise a ranking, and we do not.

Do you have an office in Fort Collins?

No. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy, Texas, and works with owners by phone, email and shared links. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
